gaps.sentence: We were deeply ___ by the news of the accident.
gaps.explanation: deeply shocked is the standard collocation for a strong negative reaction to news.

gaps.sentence: The judge ___ the verdict after four hours of deliberation.
gaps.explanation: 'Deliver a verdict/judgement' is the legal collocation.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: Students should ___ attention when the teacher is speaking.
gaps.explanation: pay attention is the fixed collocation for listening or concentrating carefully.

gaps.sentence: Her company ___ a huge profit last year.
gaps.explanation: make a profit (or make a loss) is the fixed business collocation.

gaps.sentence: He ___ a serious accident on his motorbike last year.
gaps.explanation: have an accident is the fixed collocation for being involved in one.

gaps.sentence: Halfway through the film, the children were fast ___.
gaps.explanation: fast asleep means completely asleep; it is the fixed collocation with 'fast'.

gaps.sentence: They ___ a lot of business with companies in Asia.
gaps.explanation: do business with somebody is the fixed expression for commercial activity.
